strategy.title: No plan until a price theatres pay is established for either offer

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is right. Neither opening has a purchase price for this buyer: cop_60befe0f62f948af82eb's $5,000 is the arts council's operating-support grant award a theatre receives, not a fee it pays for drafting; cop_28951609e7744b16851c's $650 is the union minimum salary for an employed stage manager, a wage floor and not a price any theatre paid for a contracted one. Brain's own OFFER_AND_PRICE link is false on both cards, and the measured agreements (6/50 and 4/40) carry no price. Recomputed what the gap decides: at an unknown price no deal count exists; the target cannot be divided into deals, so neither volume (210 directory companies, 160-170 un-asked) nor conversion (12% and 10%) nor settlement (7-10 days) can make a plan without it. If the stage manager sold at $650, 7 weeks = $4,550 gross from ~17 expected acceptances at 10% of 170, with $500/week Cue Line cost — feasible — but that price is not established, so decisiveLinks = [OFFER_AND_PRICE] is the decisive gap and not a constraint. The resolution is actionable: recover the agreed prices from the 10 recorded acceptances first (records, not a live test — which is why this is NO_PLAN rather than CONDITIONAL), then quote a stated price above the $500 cost and record written acceptances.
findings: The fallback quote should state the price, the sample (a subset of un-asked contacts), the acceptance count that proves it and a stop rule, and should note that the measured 4/40 and 6/50 conversion rates were taken at an unknown price, so conversion at the quoted price is re-measured by the same test.

For the stage-manager offer, the plan should require Cue Line's payment terms to fall after the theatre pays, or exposure exceeds the $0 cap; peakFundingCents 0 on the card is the only evidence of that.
